newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek stocks lose 0.49pct, seen in range.
newsitem.headline: Greek stocks lose 0.49pct, seen in range.

text.p: Greek shares were unable to hold on to mid-session gains on Wednesday when the index peaked above 1,600 points. They finished 0.49 percent lower.
Fund managers said equities showed weakness after bouncing back from the upper limit of the index's trading range.

"There is continuing validation that the benchmark index is in a trading range between 1,500 and 1,630 points since June when the market completed a correction from its late May highs," said Alexandros Sarrigeorgiou, fund manager at Allianz mutual funds.
Equities turned back after running into a critical technical level around 1,640-1,650 points with lower volume than what is needed to climb higher, he added.

"This trading behaviour, and for that matter the performance of the market throughout 1997, is a healthy reaction," said Sarrigeorgiou. "The stock market needs confirmation on the return of consumer price inflation to a clear downward path."
Stock prices were seen rising later this year, helped by a cocktail of positive factors.
"The index will break out of its current levels in the coming months as market participants witness strong profit growth in 1997 and start looking at 1998 forecasts," said Sarrigeorgiou.
"But this may fall through if the 1998 budget is not drafted along the lines of the convergence programme."
The Bank of Greece lifted remaining foreign exchange controls allowing Greek residents and legal entities to hold foreign exchange deposits with local credit institutions effective August 1.
The Athens general index finished a net 0.49 percent or 7.84 points off Tuesday's 1,592.01 close at 1,584.17, easing from a mid-session high of 1,604.33 points.
Turnover was slack, amounting to 10.4 billion drachmas on volume of 3.4 million shares.
Decliners beat advancers 122 to 85 with 20 shares unchanged on 227 traded.
OTE telecom Global Depository Shares (GDS) were quoted on London's SEAQ International market at $10.6-$10.8. Two GDSs make up one share of OTE.
The Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 3,800 drachmas, capped at 5,000 drachmas, was quoted at 1,123-1,153 drachmas.

The recently launched second Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 6,800 drachmas, capped at 10,000 drachmas, was quoted at 1,049-1,109 drachmas. The warrants expire December 16, 1998. Shares of the underlying stock were down 25 drachmas at 6,240.
The Merrill Lynch American call warrant on a basket of 23 Greek equities that are part of the Athens general index was quoted at 639.42-680.23 drachmas. The warrants expire January 9 1998.

The ING Baring Financial Products American style call warrant based on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted at $72.92-$75.70. The strike price is set at $99.60 and the warrants expire October 8, 1997.

The ING Baring Financial Products American-style call warrant on a basket of six blue-chips denominated in drachmas was quoted at 3,307-3,527 drachmas. The strike price is set at 10,000 drachmas and the warrants expire on February 2, 1998.
The ING Baring American-style second call warrant on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted at $11.63 bid/no offer. The strike price is set at $110.0 and the warrants expire April 9 1998.

The recently launched ING Baring American-style, drachma- denominated call warrant on the bourse's benchmark index was quoted at 223-254 drachmas. The strike price is set at 1,639 points and the warrants expire May 14 1998. --Angelos Kiosklis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
